title: Representation Function r_A(n)
content: The representation function $r_A(n)$ counts ordered pairs $(a,b) \in A \times A$ with $a + b = n$. Each unordered pair $\{a,b\}$ with $a \neq b$ contributes 2; diagonal pairs $(a,a)$ contribute 1. Three variants are defined: repFunc (ordered, on sets), repFuncUnordered (a ≤ b), and repFuncFinset (ordered, on Finsets for computability).
mathContext: $r_A(n) = |\{(a,b) \in A \times A : a + b = n\}|$. The Erdős-Turán conjecture concerns $\limsup_{n \to \infty} r_A(n)$. The unordered variant: $r_A^{\text{unord}}(n) = |\{(a,b) : a+b=n, a \leq b, a,b \in A\}|$.

title: Asymptotic Basis of Order 2
content: A ⊆ ℕ is an asymptotic basis of order 2 if A + A ⊇ {n : n ≥ N₀} for some threshold N₀. Equivalently, (A+A)^c is finite. The equivalence (isAsymptoticBasis_iff) uses csSup from Mathlib: the finite complement has a maximum, giving the threshold. Two formulations allow flexibility in proofs — the threshold form for density arguments, the cofinite form for structural ones.
mathContext: $A + A \supseteq [N_0, \infty)$ iff $(A+A)^c$ is finite. Examples: $\mathbb{N}$ (basis of order 1), squares (Lagrange: order 4). An *exact* basis satisfies $A + A = \mathbb{N}$.

title: Sidon Sets and Bounded Representation
content: A Sidon set (B₂ sequence) has all pairwise sums distinct: if a+b = c+d with a,b,c,d ∈ A, then {a,b} = {c,d}. Introduces IsSidon, proves sidon_repFunc_bounded (r_A(n) ≤ 2 for all n), and establishes finiteness of representation sets. Sidon sets, introduced by Simon Sidon (1932) in harmonic analysis, are the extremal case of thin representation — they have the minimum possible r_A among non-trivial sets.
mathContext: For Sidon $A$: $r_A(n) \leq 2$ for all $n$. Proof: any $(c,d)$ with $c+d=n$ satisfies $\{c,d\} = \{a,b\}$ for any fixed representation $(a,b)$, so the representation set $\subseteq \{(a,b),(b,a)\}$. The Sidon density bound $|A \cap [0,N]| = O(\sqrt{N})$ is tight (greedy construction achieves it).

title: The Erdős-Turán Conjecture ($500 Prize)
content: Three variants formalized: erdos_turan_weak (∀ k, ∃ n, r_A(n) > k — the representation function is unbounded), erdos_turan_strong (lim sup r_A(n)/log(n) > 0 — logarithmic growth), and erdos_28 (the prize problem wrapping the weak form). Erdős and Turán posed this in 1941 after studying Waring's problem. No 'thin basis' with bounded r_A is known; the conjecture asserts none exists.
mathContext: Weak: $\forall k \in \mathbb{N}, \exists n, r_A(n) > k$. Strong: $\limsup_{n \to \infty} r_A(n)/\log(n) > 0$. Both remain open after 80+ years. Prize: \$500.

title: Known Partial Results (Axiomatized)
content: Axiomatizes two landmark results: Grekos, Haddad, Helou, Pihko (2003) proved r_A(n) ≥ 6 infinitely often via combinatorial averaging — if r_A(n) ≤ 5 for all large n, a counting contradiction arises. Borwein et al. later pushed the bound to 8. The progression 6 → 8 → ... → ∞ (conjectured) represents decades of hard work. These are axioms since formalizing the proofs requires substantial analytic machinery beyond current Mathlib.
mathContext: Grekos (2003): $r_A(n) \geq 6$ for infinitely many $n$. Borwein: $r_A(n) \geq 8$ for infinitely many $n$. The gap between 8 and $\infty$ is the remaining challenge.

title: Concrete Examples: Even Numbers and ℕ
content: Proves the even numbers form a basis for even integers with r_{2ℕ}(2n) = n/2 + 1 unordered pairs. Shows ℕ is a trivial basis with r_ℕ^{unord}(n) = n/2 + 1, giving r_ℕ(n) → ∞ — the conjecture holds trivially for ℕ. These examples ground the abstract theory: they show representation functions can grow linearly, and the conjecture's content lies in ruling out sublinear growth for all bases.
mathContext: For $A = \mathbb{N}$: $r_{\mathbb{N}}^{\text{unord}}(n) = \lfloor n/2 \rfloor + 1$ (pairs $(k, n-k)$ for $k \leq n/2$). For $A = 2\mathbb{N}$: $A+A = 2\mathbb{N}$, $r_{2\mathbb{N}}(2n) = n+1$.

title: Sidon Set Density Bound via Erdős #340
content: Imports the Erdős #340 Sidon upper bound via a bridge lemma converting Set-based IsSidon to Finset-based Erdos340.IsSidon. Proves sidon_density_bound: |A∩[0,N]| ≤ √(2N)+1 for Sidon A. Key technical results: card_upper_triangle bounds the number of distinct sums by C(|F|+1,2), and finset_sumset_card_bound chains this with the sumset definition.
mathContext: $|A \cap [0,N]| \leq \sqrt{2N} + 1$ for Sidon $A$. Proof uses $|\text{sumset}(F)| \leq \binom{|F|+1}{2}$ (each sum from a unique unordered pair) and $\text{Erdos340.sidon\_upper\_bound}$.

title: Sidon Sets Cannot Be Asymptotic Bases
content: The structural crown jewel: no infinite Sidon set is an asymptotic basis. Proof by contradiction with explicit numerics: if A is a Sidon basis with threshold N₀, choose N = (4N₀+100)². Coverage gives N-N₀+1 ≤ |sumset(A_N)| ≤ |A_N|(|A_N|+1)/2. The Sidon density bound gives |A_N| ≤ 5N₀+126. Expanding: (5N₀+126)(5N₀+127)/2 ≥ (4N₀+100)²-N₀+1, which reduces to 7N₀²+333N₀+4000 ≤ 0 — impossible. This proves the key incompatibility: bounded representation (r_A ≤ 2) and basis coverage are structurally irreconcilable.
mathContext: Set $N = (4N_0+100)^2$. Coverage: $N-N_0+1 \leq \binom{|A_N|+1}{2}$. Sidon: $|A_N| \leq \sqrt{2N}+1 \leq 5N_0+126$. Combining: $7N_0^2 + 333N_0 + 4000 \leq 0$ — contradiction for all $N_0 \geq 0$.

title: Basis Density Lower Bound: √N
content: Proves basis_element_count_sq: |A∩[0,N]|² ≥ N-N₀+1 for any asymptotic basis. The proof chains: [N₀,N] ⊆ sumset(A∩[0,N]) → |[N₀,N]| ≤ |sumset(S)| ≤ |S|². This √N lower bound matches the Sidon density upper bound exactly — a beautiful duality in additive combinatorics: bases are at least as dense as Sidon sets are at most.
mathContext: $N - N_0 + 1 = |[N_0,N]| \leq |\text{sumset}(S)| \leq |S|^2$ where $S = A \cap [0,N]$. Hence $|A \cap [0,N]| \geq \sqrt{N - N_0 + 1} \sim \sqrt{N}$. The $\sqrt{N}$ threshold: minimum for bases, maximum for Sidon sets.
